name: build-fork
title: Build-Fork ✦ Orbit Console
description: Programmable AI developer console — Python SDK, Rust job server, Next.js terminal UI, IPFS versioning, and a full MCP server that also enters this console into the fleet's arenas.

logo_module.why: the mark in this console's header is not build-fork's state — it belongs to whoever owns this module, so it lives in the logo module and every change is a signature by the address in the `owner` field above. This process forwards that signature and cannot mint one.
logo_module.read: GET /build-fork/api/logo — public, cached at ~/.mod/build-fork/logo-cache.json so a sleeping logo module cannot blank the header
logo_module.write: POST /build-fork/api/logo with `x-mod-token: <mod-protocol token>` alongside the console bearer

/system/htop.docs: htop-grade hardware stats: per-core CPU, mem/swap/disk, full process table with users + cmdlines. Owner-only — raw cmdlines can leak secrets passed as CLI args. Rendered by the SYSTEM tab in the app's Account sidebar.

/folders.docs: List folders under a path with optional search filter

/suggest_folders.docs: Suggest folders using embedcode similarity search

/jobs.docs: Submit a job (auth) or list ALL jobs (public — tasks form a public code ledger)

/jobs/{id}.docs: Get any job by id (public ledger; shareable via QR deep link ?job={id}) or delete your own job (auth)

/jobs/{id}/stream.docs: SSE live stream of job output (public ledger)

/kill.docs: Kill a process by PID or port (owner-only; requires x-sudo signature bound to pid:/port:)

/modules/{name}/process.docs: Manage a module's processes — body {action: status|stop|start|restart, target?: api|app}. Backend is pluggable per module (pm2|systemd|generic) via MOD_PM env or the target module's config.json `process_manager` field (default: auto-detect). Modules shipping a flake.nix/shell.nix get self-launched commands nix-wrapped. Owner-only; status is read-only, and mutating actions on a module other than build-fork require an x-sudo signature bound to process:{name}. Response includes the resolved `backend` and `nix_env`.

/files/write.docs: Write a file. Untrusted callers are confined to their workspace; trusted callers (owner + whitelisted editors) may write anywhere under ~/mod (incl. core/+orbit/) with just their bearer session — no per-write sudo.

/modules/{name}.docs: Delete a module. Editing a module not personally owned by the caller requires an x-sudo signature from the owner key.

/modules/{name}/restore.docs: Restore a module from a snapshot CID (owner-only; x-sudo required for modules other than build-fork).

/modules/{name}/mr-fork.docs: Fork a module into the caller's sandboxed workspace, pinned to a base snapshot CID. Any signed-in user; body {refresh?: bool}.

/modules/{name}/merge-requests.docs: List merge requests for a module (public ledger) or open one: {title, description?, head_cid?, base_cid?, message?}. Defaults to snapshotting the caller's fork; raw head_cid makes the MR fully CID-native.

/merge-requests.docs: All merge requests across modules (public ledger).

/merge-requests/{id}.docs: One merge request; lazily folds a finished merge job back into the record (merged/merge_failed + merged_cid).

/merge-requests/{id}/diff.docs: Changed files (base→head) + conflict set vs the CURRENT live tree, computed from snapshot manifests.

/merge-requests/{id}/comment.docs: Comment on an MR: {body, action?: approve|request_changes}. Verdicts require a trusted reviewer (owner or whitelist) and move the MR status.

/merge-requests/{id}/update.docs: Author pushes a new revision: {head_cid?, message?} (re-snapshots their fork by default); reopens a changes_requested MR.

/merge-requests/{id}/close.docs: Close an MR (author or trusted reviewer).

/merge-requests/{id}/merge.docs: AGENTIC MERGE (owner-only): auto-snapshots the live tree, stages base+head from their CIDs, and submits an agent job that three-way merges base/head/live semantically. Body {instructions?, model?}. The job's completion snapshot becomes merged_cid.

/suggestions.docs: Every suggestion across the orbit (public ledger, minus private modules). Filters: ?module=&status=&author=.

/modules/{name}/suggestions.docs: One module's suggestion queue (public) or file a suggestion: {title, body?}. Any signed-in caller — no fork, no CID, no diff. Capped at 20 open per author per module.

/suggestions/{id}.docs: Get one suggestion (folds in a finished play job) or delete it — an admin of the module, or its author while it is still unplayed.

/suggestions/{id}/comments.docs: The ENTIRE discussion on one suggestion, oldest first. List responses carry only the last 20 comments of a thread plus `comment_count` — commenting needs no account, so threads grow without a gate — and this is the call that holds one whole. No paging and no `since`: a reader refreshes the lot.

/suggestions/{id}/comment.docs: Add to a suggestion's discussion: {body}. Open to ANYONE — no wallet, no whitelist, no association with the module; unsigned callers post under a stable anon: handle derived from their IP. The weakest write on this API: it appends text an admin must read and act on, and cannot vote, triage or reach the tree. Returns the whole refreshed thread. The discussion rides along in the brief if the suggestion is ever played, marked as untrusted and length-capped.

/suggestions/{id}/vote.docs: Second a suggestion, or take it back — a toggle, so the count is people. The open queue sorts by it.

/suggestions/{id}/status.docs: Triage: {status: open|rejected|done, note?}. Admin of the module only (owner or scoped editor). playing/played are set by playing it.

/suggestions/{id}/play.docs: PLAY IT AS AN EDIT (admin-only): submits an agent job in the live module under the ADMIN's own account and credentials, with the suggestion as its brief. Body {instructions?, prompt?, model?} — instructions ride on top of the suggestion and outrank it; prompt replaces the generated brief. No sudo signature: it is the same power as typing the edit yourself, so the contributor's text never writes to the tree by itself. Snapshots + rolls back like any other edit.

/agent/auth.docs: The caller's per-agent connection state (claude live; codex/agent slots reserved) plus the server's fallback credential source. Tracked in the app's Account sidebar AGENT tab.

/agent/auth/{agent}.docs: Connect (POST {token, refresh_token?, expires_at?, source?}) or forget (DELETE) the caller's own session for one agent. Jobs the caller submits then run on their account instead of the server's. For claude there are two ways in: the console's "Log in with Claude" button (claude.ai OAuth, run by the app's /api/credentials/oauth route, which posts the result here — those sessions carry a refresh token and are renewed by the job runner), or pasting the sk-ant-oat… output of `claude setup-token` (an sk-ant-api… key works too). Stored per-wallet in ~/.mod/build-fork/agent_auth/ (0600).

/whitelist.docs: List edit-whitelist (GET, public) or add an address (POST, owner-only). Whitelisted addresses are trusted editors: owner-level EDIT access to the orbit (host filesystem, unsandboxed jobs, core/+orbit/ writes), but NOT owner-only powers (whitelist mgmt, set_owner, kill, delete/rename/restore). Stored off-tree in ~/.mod/build-fork/whitelist.json.

/whitelist/{address}.docs: Remove an address from the edit whitelist (owner-only).

/mcp.docs: MCP Streamable HTTP, JSON-RPC 2.0. initialize / tools/list / tools/call / resources/* / prompts/*, single messages or batches. Every tool re-enters the REST surface carrying this request's own Authorization header, so MCP and the browser get the same gate and the same errors — anonymous callers get exactly the [public] tools. GET returns the tool list and transport notes.

/arena.docs: Where this console is entered as a competitor, and every arena/1.0 module it can see. Never returns the shared key.

/arena/solve.docs: What a coding arena calls when this console is entered: {task|prompt, language?, mode?} in, {code, language} out. Runs a real agent job per call, so it is default-deny — refused with 403 until the owner runs arena_enter, and 401 without the key minted at that moment.

/arena/play.docs: What a game arena calls: {view, seat?, prompt?} in, {move} out. Same gate as /arena/solve. One agent job per move — expect seconds per turn.

mcp.stdio: build-fork-jobs --stdio  (bridges to the running API; BUILD_FORK_TOKEN acts as you)
mcp.auth: the same Authorization: Bearer token the REST routes take; without one you get the tools tagged [public]

arena.discovery: every module on this fleet whose config.json declares protocol arena/*
arena.default: off; owner runs arena_enter, which mints the key and switches the endpoints on
